To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a method for hyper-local geotagging of non-geotaged content items that is accurate enough for most practical applications, that the accuracy of this approach varies significantly across different types of content, and that the best results can be achieved by modeling and predicting location according to source of the content item.

we can assign locations to short text items shared via social media by modeling the location distribution of n-grams, that the accuracy of this assignment depends on the size of the n-grams and that it can be improved by modeling location distributions separately for different sources of content.

(a) a data-driven approach is able to assign location to a large fraction of short social media texts (up to 80%); (b) this assignment can be done at a hyper-local level, with accuracy that varies across locations; (c) the approach is more accurate for short texts than longer ones; and (d) it is preferable to predict location for each content item according to its source
